Óscar Arias Sánchez is a Costa Rican statesman, president from 1986 to 1990 and again from 2006 to 2010. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987 for his plan to end the wars of Central America.

When he took office, civil wars were raging in Nicaragua, El Salvador and Guatemala, and the United States was arming the Contras from Honduras. Arias proposed a plan for ceasefires, amnesty, free elections and an end to outside aid to rebels. The five Central American presidents signed it in Guatemala in August 1987, in the talks named after the town of Esquipulas.

The plan opened the way to elections in Nicaragua in 1990 and peace deals in El Salvador and Guatemala in the 1990s. It also made Costa Rica known abroad as a country of peace, the face of the nation that had abolished its army.
